assessments.rationale: Provisional mapping is supported by the NAICS definition covering mine-site development, mining and beneficiation of copper, nickel, lead and zinc ores, including concentrates. Uncertainty for unestablished dimensions is retained through unknown labels and a gap, so no material boundary disagreement.

Identity card and source record identify mining of lead and zinc ore and frozen industry-product evidence links that product to NAICS 212230. Provisional status appropriately reflects that the product record alone does not establish all operating dimensions.

Identity card and source record identify mining of copper and nickel ore and frozen industry-product evidence links it to NAICS 212230. Provisional mapping with an explicit gap is consistent with the incomplete buyer, delivery, workforce, economics and workflow evidence.

Proposal boundary follows the frozen NAICS job and excludes gold and adjacent services; gold-product evidence is used only as counterevidence for the exclusion, not as supporting evidence. Seven dimensions are stated with fact, inference or unknown labels and explicit exclusions, supporting a provisional rather than overstated proposal.

Candidate is an unvalidated prior-model seed labeled Mining and geological engineering. Frozen evidence has no candidate-specific operating definition and mapping evidence reports no sufficient match; unresolved with a gap correctly avoids treating missing evidence as affirmative non-mapping.

NAICS definition directly covers operating industrial-grade sand pits, dredging for industrial-grade sand and washing, screening or otherwise preparing it. Provisional mapping appropriately preserves uncertainty for buyer, delivery, workforce, economics and workflow dimensions not established by the frozen records.

Frozen product identity is quarrying industrial glass sand for melting only and is linked by industry-product evidence to NAICS 212322. Provisional mapping to the industrial-sand proposal is evidence-supported without claiming a complete operating-market boundary.

Frozen product identity is quarrying industrial molding sand and is linked to the industrial-sand NAICS anchor. Provisional status is appropriate because the descriptive product record does not establish every operating-identity dimension.

Frozen product identity covers other industrial sand including grinding, blast, furnace, engine, filtration and oil uses and is linked to NAICS 212322. Provisional mapping does not expand the boundary into downstream customer manufacturing and retains explicit gaps.

Proposal follows the NAICS extraction and preparation job and the three industrial-sand product identities, excludes construction-grade gravel and water-resource construction, and labels unestablished dimensions unknown. Its provisional confidence and research gaps are consistent with the frozen evidence.
